subject.title: [Bug]: Unscheduled reminder guard fires for isolated-session crons + counter lost during compaction

question: Should maintainers adopt or refresh the open fork PR that closes this issue, land the same-repo partial PR first, or open a target-repo replacement covering both reported gaps?
rationale: The bug is source-proven, but there is already an exact conflicting fork PR plus a same-repo partial PR, so automation should not queue a duplicate until maintainers choose the ownership path.

options.title: Adopt Or Replace Full Fix
options.body: Use the fork PR as source material or open a narrow target-repo replacement covering both isolated-cron matching and compaction-counter preservation with regression tests.

options.title: Land Partial Compaction Fix First
options.body: Proceed with the same-repo compaction PR while keeping this issue open for the isolated-session cron gap.

options.title: Wait On Fork Refresh
options.body: Keep this issue paired with the fork PR and wait for the contributor to resolve conflicts, proof, and failing checks.

recommendation.title: Adopt Or Replace Full Fix
recommendation.body: Use the fork PR as source material or open a narrow target-repo replacement covering both isolated-cron matching and compaction-counter preservation with regression tests.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged the prior active-cron suppression and recently touched the current guard/runtime surface, making them the best available routing owner for the adopt-or-replace choice.
